metadata.case_name: CHEUNG LUK v. LO KWOK HUNG

injuries.description: fractured wrist resulting in radial displacement of left hand.
source: man of 75 - fractured wrist resulting in radial displacement of left hand.

Dr. Wedderburn examined him early in May 1980 and again in February 1982. He found that there was evidence of a fracture of the left forearm which had obviously been treated by a plaster-cast, and hospital records showed that he was discharged after three days and that he had to wear the plaster for about 40 days.
The hand was displaced towards the thumb side slightly at the wrist. He described this at a radial displacement.

The fracture went up the radius and its closest point to the wrist was one inch; and the fracture was oblique across the bone. The distal fragment was tilted forward by 10°. The other bone of the forearm was dislocated so that the normal mechanism of the right wrist joint was severely affected.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture at wrist or hand level

manifestations.description: Lost 40° of the movement of extending the left hand at the wrist (May 1980).
Radial deviation normal but ulnar deviation reduced to 15° (May 1980); later ulnar deviation improved to 20° (Feb 1982).
Area of the wrist on the left hand appeared more swollen than that on the right.
Grip strength initially 25 lb in left hand and 70 lb in right hand (May 1980); later 40 lb left and 55 lb right (Feb 1982).
Distal fragment tilted forward by 10°; other bone of the forearm dislocated affecting wrist mechanism.
Unable to return to work because of weakness of the wrist; doctor considered that at his age he was not fit for work.
Impairment estimates: initially 10% impairment of the arm (6% of the whole man) based on 5% impairment from loss of ulnar deviation; later impairment of the arm decreased to 8% (5% of the whole man).

treatments_received: physiotherapy (three times a week for some time after the accident, later monthly)

losses.description: Reduced function of the left wrist and left hand including loss of extension, reduced ulnar deviation, reduced grip strength and residual anatomical abnormality after fracture and displacement.
Unable to return to work as a cook due to weakness of the wrist; doctors considered at his age he could not seek or undertake other lower paid work.
